gen-gf-autour-one-gf-ubuntu-sans: Round, loud letters with a smooth runway into every curve. Autour One does the shouting while Ubuntu Sans, with its big-eyed lowercase and pipe-like strokes, stays quietly modern underneath.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-armata: Tall, bold lowercase that nearly stands as high as its capitals. Gugi holds full-width stroke joins where Armata, the sans-serif body, leaves spacious gaps between characters, and that difference is the pair.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-liter: Tall lowercase, cut-open terminals, and a bold stance. Liter draws with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on its rounds, giving the Gugi heading a quiet place to land.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-miriam-libre: Tall, bold and cut open. Gugi's lowercase nearly climbs to its capitals, built to be noticed, while Miriam Libre, a sans-serif, keeps thin wire-like strokes and a sturdy lowercase.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Bold letters, cut wide open. Gugi earns its keep big and brief, where its tall lowercase shows off, while Mochiy Pop P One leaves wide gaps between its letters.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads with big open counters and curved strokes that stop before they turn inward. Gugi, with its rope-fine strokes, is best loud and distinctive, while the body is best at keeping text modern and clean.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Tall, cut-open lowercase with a bold, distinctive look. Noto Sans Brahmi keeps a high mean line and open-ended curves, so extended reading should feel light and unhurried beside Gugi.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads gently, its strokes tapering off before they touch. Gugi cuts its letters at a single depth, so the text underneath, with barely any step down from capitals, moves through paragraphs without snagging.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Smooth, bold curves with no swelling where they meet the stems. Noto Sans Ugaritic does the quieter job, keeping capitals and lowercase close in height with open letter mouths, while Gugi handles the loud, display work.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-stack-sans-text: Goldman sets wide, commanding letters with generous clearance. Stack Sans Text draws a marker-like constant line with well-separated curve endings, so its plain sans text moves along without friction.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-noto-san: Love Ya Like A Sister has bold, low-slung ascenders and a level beat. Noto Sans Cherokee follows with tall letters and short stalks, so a long passage feels like pulling one steady thread.
Noto Sans Mono spaces its letters generously so none bump, with every curve opening wide, a sans-serif that feels contemporary. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its keep big and brief.

Love Ya Like A Sister draws round letters like bent wire, loud and low. Noto Sans Mro sits beneath it with dense, tall-looking words and generous openings into every letter, which is the quality that holds the two together.
Bold neon glass, reshaped into letters. Love Ya Like A Sister makes the splash with that tubular stroke, while Noto Sans Old Italic keeps its curve endings well apart.
Noto Sans Tai Viet has short ascenders and a tall x-height, its terminals pulled back before each curve closes. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its place large and brief.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-stack-sans-text: Stack Sans Text draws a marker-like line with curve endings held apart. Gugi does its boldest, most distinctive work up top, while the body font's big-bodied lowercase handles the quieter text.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-batak: Wide-tracked curves that refuse to close, quietly level. Offside stretches out untapered up top, whereas Noto Sans Batak brings a towering x-height and an e that never squeezes shut.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Expressive and commanding, Offside spreads its open-ended curves wide across the line. Offside excels at a level, wide-set statement, while Noto Sans Glagolitic keeps sturdy lowercase friendly and legible at small sizes.
